title: Place
description: Somewhere events happen. A place is a geographic fact, not a historiographical argument, so it needs no source: sources may be empty here, as on region and source records (rule 6). names[0] is the display name and the rest are variants and other-language forms; that the list is non-empty is rule 18, because the keyword subset has no minItems. region is an override, as on an event: it is derived from where at index time.

names.description: The display name first, then variants: "Lisbon", "Lisboa".

where.description: The point itself. Required: a place with no coordinates is a word, and an event that wants one is placeless instead.

regionNote.description: Why the lane on this record is an override rather than the derivation. Written only beside a `region`, and only by whatever set it: the import writes it because a placeless event or a place whose own point reaches no polygon has to be given a lane, and a lane given by a tool is not the same fact as one derived from a coordinate (health review A, finding 23a). A person writing an override says why here too, in a sentence.

summary.description: Optional, and written by a person when it is there: what this place is, in a sentence or two.
